_comment: Pinned upstream sources for libarchive and everything linked into it.
This file is the single source of truth for EVERY platform's build, and that
is the whole reason it is a file rather than a literal inside one build
script. This repository exists so that a CVE in zlib, bzip2, liblzma or
libzstd can be answered without cutting an XeFM release; if each platform
carried its own copy of these versions, the failure mode would be bumping
zlib for Windows and shipping the old one everywhere else. Bump it here,
rebuild each platform, cut one release.
Pinned by version AND sha256: a release asset that changes under an
unchanged tag is exactly what the hash is here to catch. Every build must
verify the hash and refuse to continue on a mismatch.
Where upstream publishes a signature, `signature_url` and `signing_key`
record how the hash below was established in the first place. See
CLAUDE.md for the procedure to repeat when bumping a version.

sources.name: zlib
sources.note: zlib publishes no detached signature for its release assets.

sources.name: bzip2
sources.note: No signature either, but this hash is the value every distribution has quoted since 2019. bzip2 has had no release since; a new version appearing is itself worth a second look.

sources.name: xz
sources.note: NEVER move this pin below 5.6.2. Versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 shipped the CVE-2024-3094 backdoor, and a downgrade is the one direction nobody would question in a diff.

sources.name: libarchive
sources.note: Built last, against the four above. Its version is what names the release assets.
